name: Prednisolone
route_note: oral tablets or soluble/liquid forms; eye drops for ocular inflammation; enemas and suppositories for proctitis
tagline: The active form of prednisone and the standard oral steroid in much of the world
summary: Prednisolone is the active glucocorticoid formed from prednisone and is itself given orally, as eye drops and rectally. It is about four times as potent as hydrocortisone with less mineralocorticoid effect, and is used across asthma, rheumatology, gastroenterology, haematology and transplantation.
mechanism: Glucocorticoids diffuse into cells and bind the cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1). The activated receptor moves to the nucleus, where it switches on anti-inflammatory genes (transactivation, e.g. annexin-1, IκBα, MKP-1) and represses pro-inflammatory transcription factors such as NF-κB and AP-1 (transrepression), reducing cytokines, prostaglandins, adhesion molecules and immune-cell activation.
The 1,2 double bond introduced into the A ring of hydrocortisone increases glucocorticoid potency and slows metabolism while reducing mineralocorticoid activity relative to cortisol.
uses: Ocular inflammation such as uveitis (eye drops)
Allergic disorders, croup and skin disease

history.title: Cortisone in arthritis
history.detail: Hench's results with cortisone prompt a search for more potent, less salt-retaining analogues.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Kendall, Hench and Reichstein share the Nobel Prize for adrenal cortex hormones.

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Nobile's team at Schering produces prednisolone from hydrocortisone by bacterial dehydrogenation.

history.title: Preschool wheeze trial
history.detail: A UK trial (NEJM 2009) finds oral prednisolone does not shorten hospital stay in preschool children with viral wheeze.

serious: adrenal suppression and adrenal crisis on abrupt withdrawal
raised intraocular pressure with eye drops

facts: Prednisolone is on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines.
Prednisolone and prednisone have essentially equivalent potency milligram for milligram.
